alert_2026_provisional: 2026 tax rates are based on official indexed amounts (AJ 2027). The proposed 40%→35% bracket reform was not enacted for income year 2026.
footer_disclaimer: Calculations are indicative. Always consult a tax advisor for your final tax return.
input_below_aow_age: I am below Dutch AOW retirement age
input_gross_salary_hint: Full gross salary as listed on your annual statement / payslip
input_workdays_other: Days worked in other country (e.g. 🇫🇷 FR)
input_workdays_other_hint: E.g. customer installations abroad. Counted the same as BE days for Belgian tax.
input_thirty_percent_ruling_hint: Expat rule: 30% of salary is tax free
input_withheld_tax_nl: NL wage tax withheld by employer (€)
input_withheld_tax_nl_hint: From your annual statement (jaaropgave). Leave 0 to skip eindafrekening.
input_sick_days_hint: Days of sick leave during the year. NL and BE calculate the sourcing ratio differently for sick days.
summary_copy_error: Copy failed. Please allow clipboard access in your browser.
be_only_residents: Belgian tax only applies to residents of Belgium.
be_no_home_working: No days worked outside the Netherlands → no Belgian income tax due on salary.
be_warning_text: This is a simplified estimate. Your final return may differ due to spouse income splitting, special social security contributions, regional taxes and other personal deductions. Consult a tax advisor for your final tax return.
years_description: This comparison uses the exact same input values (salary, workdays, family status), only the selected tax year changes.
input_workdays_total_zero_warning: Enter at least one workday to calculate a realistic net/day amount.
input_workdays_total_high_warning: This seems high; please double-check if all day counts are correct.
wfh_description: Sweeps the NL ↔ BE day split while keeping total workdays fixed. Hover to inspect each scenario.
wfh_x_label: Days worked from home in 🇧🇪 BE (%)
wfh_qualifying_taxpayer_note: ≤10% BE (≥90% NL): you qualify as a 'kwalificerend buitenlands belastingplichtige'. Benefits: hypotheekrenteaftrek (mortgage interest deduction), aftrek ziektekosten (medical expenses), and heffingskorting niet-werkende partner (non-working partner credit). Requires an inkomensverklaring validated by Belgian tax authorities and sent to the Dutch Belastingdienst.
wfh_threshold_25_hint: Above this: Belgian income tax applies
wfh_hover_hint: Hover the chart to explore scenarios
summary_sourcing_nl_formula: NL method: (NL + sick days) ÷ (NL + BE + other + sick days) — sick days count as NL workdays
summary_sourcing_be_formula: BE method: NL days ÷ (NL + BE + other days) — sick days excluded from both numerator and denominator
summary_sourcing_overlap_note: ⚠️ With sick days and Belgian workdays recorded, the NL and BE sourcing fractions can sum to more than 100%: NL counts sick days as NL-sourced workdays, while BE excludes them entirely — making the BE fraction slightly larger than it would be otherwise. The overlap equals sick days × BE days ÷ [(NL + BE + sick) × (NL + BE)], which may result in a small portion of sick-day income being taxed by both countries (double taxation).
wfh_threshold_49_hint: Above this: Dutch social security no longer applies. Request kaderakkoord at SVB to stay covered (applies up to 49%).
wfh_kaderakkoord_note: Working 25–49% of your days from Belgium (telework): Dutch social security remains applicable if you apply for the kaderakkoord at SVB (requires an A1 document). Above 49%, Belgian social security applies.
input_workdays_nl_hint: Include: office days, training days, offsites, and business travel days. Exclude: vacation, ADV/compensation days, national holidays, and sick leave (enter sick days separately below). Overtime and commuting do not count.
input_workdays_typical: Tip: start from 260 days (52 × 5), then subtract vacation days, ADV/compensation days, and public holidays that fall on weekdays.
input_social_security_kaderakkoord: Kaderakkoord zone (25–49% BE days): Dutch social security remains applicable if you hold an A1 certificate. Request this jointly with your employer at SVB.
input_social_security_above_50: Above 49% BE days: Belgian social security would apply. Review your working arrangement.
ref_overview_subtitle: Practical reference sheets on fiscal and social rules for cross-border workers between Belgium and the Netherlands.
ref_overview_ss_desc: Day count, FOD formula, 49% telework threshold, NL tax rates 2026 and a worked example.
ref_overview_pension_desc: AOW, ANW, RVU, Belgian retirement pension, deductions, pension penalty/bonus and border worker pension.
ref_ss_hero_subtitle: Reference guide for cross-border workers living in Belgium and working in the Netherlands. Based on ACV Information Session 24 March 2026 & Border Worker Checklist 2026.
ref_ss_be_codes_title: Belgian personal income tax declaration codes:
ref_ss_tax_vs_ss_body: For social security there is a framework agreement that neutralises remote work (up to 49%). For tax there is no comparable rule. Every day working from home in Belgium is a day on which Belgium levies tax.
ref_ss_footer: Based on ACV Border Workers Checklist 2026 & Information Session 24 March 2026 (Pelt). No rights can be derived. Consult ACV Border Workers or a tax specialist for your personal situation.
ref_pension_hero_subtitle: Reference guide on AOW, ANW, supplementary pension (NL) and Belgian retirement pension for those living in Belgium and working in the Netherlands. Based on ACV Information Session 24 March 2026 (Pelt).
ref_pension_s_aow_work: AOW & Additional Work — Points of attention
ref_pension_term_confusion_body: "Pension" in the Netherlands = supplementary to AOW (2nd pillar). "Pension" in Belgium = the statutory pension. Don't confuse this when talking to HR or pension funds.
ref_pension_footer: Based on ACV Border Workers Information Session 24 March 2026 (Pelt). No rights can be derived. Consult ACV Border Workers or a pension specialist.
ref_ss_s1_intro: Based on the double taxation treaty BE–NL the following applies:
ref_ss_s1_formula:
Telework day in Belgium  →  taxing rights: BELGIUM
Office day in Netherlands →  taxing rights: NETHERLANDS
ref_ss_s1_tip_20pct: 20% rule: If you work more than 20% of a day from home, that day counts as a full telework day for Belgian tax purposes.
ref_ss_s1_tip_60_40: Safe ratio: 60/40 — 60% office (NL) / 40% home (BE) is in principle "safe": you retain the right to mortgage interest deduction in the Netherlands (requires at least 90% NL income).
ref_ss_s1_warn_qualification: If you lose the "qualification" (less than 90% NL), the mortgage interest deduction in NL falls away. You may still be able to use the housing bonus (BE, loan before 2020).
ref_ss_s2_intro: The Netherlands and Belgium use a different method for calculating the pro-rata allocation.
ref_ss_s2_row1_be: Same, but ALSO minus sick days
ref_ss_s2_row2_be: Same (NL share after deducting sick days)
ref_ss_s2_row3_be: Removed from both numerator and denominator
ref_ss_s2_warn: Sick days increase your Belgian tax share. Example: 50 telework days, 25 sick days → NL fraction drops from 180/230 to 155/205. The share taxable in Belgium rises proportionally. Risk of double taxation!
ref_ss_s2_tip: Filing order: submit the NL return first, then calculate the BE return based on the actual amounts due.
ref_ss_s3_intro: The FPS Finance uses the following 3-step method for the Belgian return in a salary split:
ref_ss_be_formula:
STEP 1 — W (base)
  W = NL taxable wage (annual statement)
    − actual social insurance premiums due (NL SI)
    − actual income tax due (after NL refund)
    + employee share supplementary pension premium  [code 1285]
    − benefit in kind company car (NL rules)
    + benefit in kind company car (BE rules)
    + fiscally exchanged gross wage (cafeteria plan)

STEP 2 — Y (taxable in Belgium)
  Y = W × (days performed in BE ÷ total days performed)

STEP 3 — Z (exempt in Belgium)
  Z = W − Y − [NL tax × (NL days ÷ total days)]
ref_ss_s3_code_1250: Total foreign professional income (= W, pro-rata)
ref_ss_s3_code_vak4_o1: Non-exempt part (= Y, taxable in BE)
ref_ss_s3_code_vak4_o2: Exempt part with progression reservation (= Z)
ref_ss_s3_code_257: Nominal NL health insurance premium + other deductions
ref_ss_s3_warn: No tool available. FPS Finance provides no tool for the BE return in a salary split. Only guidance: MOTIV (fgov.be).
ref_ss_vv_footnote: SI = social insurance premiums (max over €38,883) · IT = income tax
ref_ss_s5_intro: Social security ≠ tax. For social security there is a framework agreement:
ref_ss_s5_row_max_telework: Max telework in country of residence (BE)
ref_ss_s5_cond1: Telework only (no other activity in BE)
ref_ss_s5_cond2: No self-employment side activity in Belgium
ref_ss_s5_cond4: Limosa declaration by employer remains mandatory
ref_ss_s6_intro: For Belgium what counts is: proof that you were physically present in the country of work (NL), not that you worked from home. Combine multiple types of evidence.
ref_ss_s6_ev2: Dated transport documents in your name (train, bus, plane)
ref_ss_s6_ev4: Hotel/car rental invoices in your name
ref_ss_s6_ev5: Minutes of meetings with attendance list
ref_ss_s6_source_note: Source: Vademecum physical presence BE–LUX (also applies to NL)
ref_ss_s7_intro: Cross-border worker, full-time, 4 days/week NL + 1 day/week home (BE). Year 2025. 6 public holidays, 25 vacation days, 50 telework days. Taxable wage €53,299.
ref_ss_s7_footnote: * €600 = municipal tax on NL net wage (6%, resident Hamont). Exact amounts depend on personal situation. Source: ACV Border Workers Information Session 24 March 2026, Pelt.
ref_ss_s8_intro: The original ACV documents on which this reference guide is based:
ref_ss_doc2_title: ACV Information Session Telework & Border Workers
ref_pension_aow_premie_sub: on max €38,883, included in wage tax
ref_pension_tip_partner: Partner coverage: a spouse without income also accrues AOW — register with SVB within one year of starting work in the Netherlands.
ref_pension_tip_aanvragen: Applying for AOW: via municipality → FPD → SVB, or via pensioenaanvraag.be or tel. 1765. At least 8 months before start date. Check periods on mijnsvb.nl (DigiD or Belgian eID).
ref_pension_anw_warn: ANW ends upon cohabiting with a partner or if the basic conditions are no longer met (e.g. child turns 18).
ref_pension_aow_work_warn: Attention — traffic light situation: anyone receiving AOW + Belgian pension + NL 2nd pillar pension who starts working in the Netherlands again becomes a health insurance member (ziekenfonds) in NL again. Consequences:
ref_pension_aow_work_li1: World income counts towards the income-dependent ZVW contribution
ref_pension_aow_work_li3: Tax burden on Belgian pension rises due to progression reservation
ref_pension_aow_work_tip: Earning alongside AOW is in itself unrestricted.
ref_pension_sup_intro: Netherlands rated best pension system in the world (Mercer 2025, NL #1 — BE #20).
ref_pension_sup_upo_sub: annual; request from provider ≥ 4 months in advance
ref_pension_sup_tip: Check pension accrual on mijnpensioenoverzicht.nl (DigiD or Belgian eID / Itsme). Older BSN? Have your sofinummer converted.
ref_pension_wtp_li1: Final-pay and average-pay schemes will be abolished
ref_pension_wtp_li2: All schemes become defined contribution schemes
ref_pension_wtp_li4: Partner pension insured as a fixed percentage
ref_pension_wtp_li5: 10% of the value can be taken as a lump sum
ref_pension_divorce_p: Pension division act on divorce: ex-partner has a statutory right to half of the pension accrued during the marriage.
ref_pension_divorce_warn: Notify the pension provider within 2 years via the 'Mededelingsformulier verdeling ouderdomspensioen bij echtscheiding'. Failure to notify = ex-partner's claim remains!
ref_pension_rvu_intro: Successor to the VUT, for heavy/physically demanding professions.
ref_pension_rvu_li1: Employee resigns → no entitlement to WW (unemployment benefit)
ref_pension_rvu_li2: Combination with Belgian retirement pension permitted
ref_pension_rvu_li3: Combination with brought-forward 2nd pillar pension permitted
ref_pension_rvu_li4: Returning to work in principle prohibited
ref_pension_rvu_tip: RVU taxation: taxable in Belgium (country of residence), unless civil servant with NL nationality. Don't forget: apply for wage tax exemption!
ref_pension_ded_intro: As a post-active cross-border worker (living BE, pension from NL):
ref_pension_ded_tip: Right to care in both the Netherlands and Belgium is retained.
ref_pension_be_warn_aanvraag: No automatic review at end of career in the Netherlands. Filing an application is mandatory if you want to retire before age 66.
ref_pension_be_tip_nl_years: Years worked in NL count towards the Belgian career requirement. 104 days in 1 year = 1 full career year (through 2026).
ref_pension_ziv_warn: AOW + Belgian pension are added together for the ZIV threshold. Also solidarity contribution: 0.5–2% for pension > €3,682 (single) / €4,212 (family).
ref_pension_be2027_intro: Career requirement per year rises from 104 → 156 effective working days (exception: 1st career year + 5 reserve days).
ref_pension_malus_intro: Applies when NOT meeting: 35 years × at least 156 days + total 7,020 performed/assimilated days.
ref_pension_bonus_intro: For those who work longer than the statutory pension age. Requires: career ≥ 35 years + 7,020 days.
ref_pension_gap_intro: Anyone who has worked a long time in the Netherlands faces a specific problem:
ref_pension_gap_li1: Belgian pension age: 66 years (2026), but AOW age: 67 years
ref_pension_gap_li2: Long NL career → low Belgian pension, early AOW impossible
ref_pension_gap_li3: Belgian unemployment benefit in principle stops at age 66
ref_pension_art64_intro: Unemployment benefit can continue until AOW age if:
ref_pension_art64_li1: At least 15 years of cross-border work proven
ref_pension_art64_li2: No pension received: temporarily waive Belgian retirement pension and do not let 2nd pillar pension commence
ref_pension_art64_warn: The arrangement does not cover all cases: those who cannot prove 15 years of cross-border work, or whose 2nd pillar pension cannot be deferred, fall outside the arrangement.
ref_pension_border_intro: The 'border worker pension' calculated a Belgian pension as if one had worked in Belgium and paid the difference. Now significantly curtailed:
ref_pension_border_li1: No new entrants for cross-border workers who become cross-border workers for the first time after 1 January 2015
ref_pension_border_li2: Early start date no longer possible — investigation aligned with statutory pension age in country of work
ref_pension_border_li3: Not only statutory NL pension (AOW) is deducted, also the supplementary (2nd pillar)
ref_pension_border_li4: Survivor pension at BE's expense remains, but also with deduction of ANW and 2nd pillar pension
ref_pension_border_tip: Did you start cross-border work before 1/1/2015? Check with FPD whether your rights to the border worker pension are preserved.
ref_pension_survivor_li1: Beneficiary in 2026: at least 51 years old
ref_pension_survivor_li3: Automatic calculation if deceased was already retired
ref_pension_survivor_li6: Combination with NL ANW / 2nd pillar pension is possible
ref_pension_survivor_sp_li2: For max 12 months: combination with replacement income possible
ref_pension_disability_intro1: With WAO/WIA benefit: no longer automatically insured for old age & death.
ref_pension_disability_li1: AOW voluntary insurance at SVB — within one year of WIA/WAO award
ref_pension_disability_li2: Or: pay regularisation contributions to FPD (BE) — to be concluded within 3 years
ref_pension_disability_intro2: With pro-rata benefit (worked in multiple countries):
ref_pension_disability_li3: Belgian waiting period: 180 days worked in 12 months before 1st sick day
ref_pension_disability_li4: With pro-rata benefit: Belgian pension accrual continues normally
ref_pension_disability_li5: Concurrence with BE invalidity benefit: Belgian law takes precedence
ref_pension_tax_intro: Main rule of the BE–NL treaty for post-active cross-border workers: tax in the country of residence (Belgium).
ref_pension_tax_exc_li1: ABP pension (civil servant) if NL nationality
ref_pension_tax_exc_li3: Carry-over 1 year for partial disability (WGA) + employment still ongoing
ref_pension_tax_exc_li4: Supplementary benefits that are not a bridge to pension
ref_pension_tax_tip1: RVU: taxable in Belgium unless civil servant with NL nationality. Declare in return as 'severance pay'. Don't forget to apply for wage tax exemption!
ref_pension_tax_tip2: AOW always taxable in Belgium (country of residence). 2nd pillar pension too, unless civil servant with exclusively NL nationality.
